title: Tenant-aware KPI ingest queue resilience and schema migration for edge gateways
creator: Lina Cho
description:
Background: Our per-request inference KPIs (latency_ms, tokens_out, model_variant, error_code) flow through an OTLP front-door and are adapted to Prometheus for long-term SLOs. We observed two recurring classes of operational failures during load spikes: 1) tenant bursts causing head-of-line blocking in the ingest queue, which results in bounded memory growth and dropped OTLP events; 2) a schema migration planned for the normalized KPI envelope (adding 'route_id' and 'cache_hit' boolean) that risks dropping unlabeled legacy envelopes during the adapter transformation.

Problem statement: We need a resilient, tenant-aware ingest pipeline for edge gateways (both hosted and dedicated) that: (a) isolates noisy tenants so one tenant's burst doesn't backpressure others; (b) persists envelopes during transient downstream outages (Prometheus adapter/DB or Kafka) with bounded local buffering and checkpointing; (c) supports a safe rolling migration of the KPI envelope schema without dropping legacy events; and (d) emits visibility metrics and tracing hooks so SRE/Platform can debug queue drain/backpressure issues.

Proposed approach summary: 1) Implement per-tenant token buckets and a soft fairness scheduler in the ingest queue sidecar to enforce burst isolation; 2) Add a small local persistent buffer (rocksdb-backed queue) with sequence checkpoints per tenant and an exponential backoff drain loop to downstream OTLP->Prom adapter; 3) Introduce a schema compatibility shim: runtime transforms add 'route_id' and 'cache_hit' when inferred from context, otherwise mark 'schema_version:legacy' and attach a compatibility flag so downstream consumers can handle both; 4) Export debug tracing spans (edge.gateway.ingest.queue.enqueue, .drain, .transform) and counters/gauges for tenant_queue_depth, tenant_dropped_events, tenant_backpressure_seconds, buffer_disk_usage; 5) Provide a migration plan (canary tenants, observability checks, automated rollback) and integration test harness that replays historical OTLP envelopes.

Why this differs from previous work: Existing metric pipeline tickets focused on fanout, rollups, and cardinality reduction. This ticket is focused on tenant isolation in the *edge ingest sidecar*, durable buffering with checkpointing, and a safe schema rollout strategy for inference KPI enrichment — cross-cutting concerns that bridge serving runtime and telemetry fabric.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant queue enforcement: bursts from one tenant should not increase queue latency for others under a 10x synthetic burst test
Durable buffer works: envelopes persist across a simulated downstream outage and are delivered once downstream recovers (tested with a 5 minute outage replay)
Schema compatibility: downstream consumers see both legacy and v1 envelopes; no unlabeled events dropped in a migration test run using 50k historical envelopes
Observability: new Prometheus metrics (tenant_queue_depth, tenant_dropped_events, tenant_backpressure_seconds, buffer_disk_usage) emit with correct labels and dashboards updated
Tracing: spans created for enqueue/drain/transform and end-to-end trace id preserved from edge to Prometheus adapter
Rollout safety: canary rollout to 3 tenants in prod with auto rollback on >1% drop or >10s increase in per-request latency SLO

2026-03-05: Design review — SRE requested explicit disk-usage guardrails and eviction policy. Added buffer_disk_usage metric and high-water eviction to writeup.
2026-03-10: Integration test harness started. Replayed 120k historical envelopes; observed 0.3% transform failures due to missing model_variant — added fallback logic.
2026-03-12: Security / privacy check — confirmed no PII in KPI envelopes; KMS not required for local queue. Noted for docs.
2026-03-14: Started canary automation script and drafted runbook. Remaining: finalize eviction policy, finish transform shim, add end-to-end tracing tests.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for queue behavior and token bucket; 2) Integration test that replays mixed-tenant traffic and asserts per-tenant fairness; 3) Chaos test: kill downstream adapter for 5 minutes and assert buffered delivery; 4) End-to-end tracing validation using distributed-trace-verify tool; 5) Canary in prod with 3 low-risk tenants for 48h, monitor metrics and error budgets
notes: SRE recommendation: set default per-tenant burst allowance to 10k events per minute with 30s refill window; allow overrides for enterprise tenants via tenant config
Potential follow-up: expose tenant QoS UI in Console for SRE/MSP teams to tune throttles
Estimate assumes existing RocksDB wrapper from ENG-772011 will be reused
